<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">WITNESS SYSTEMS,&nbsp;INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)<br> December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Court
held a claim construction hearing and issued a claim construction order on June&nbsp;8,
2005. The case will now proceed to expert discovery and summary judgment
phases.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;20, 2004, STS
Software Systems Ltd. (&#147;STS Software&#148;), a wholly-owned subsidiary of
NICE&nbsp;Systems, Ltd. (&#147;NICE Ltd.&#148;), filed a patent infringement suit in the
U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York against us (&#147;New York
Action&#148;). The New York Action asserts that our products, including eQuality
ContactStore for IP, infringe United States (&#147;U.S.). Patent No.&nbsp;6,122,665
(&#147;the &#145;665 patent&#148;) and seeks only injunctive, not monetary, relief. On the
same day, we filed a declaratory judgment action against STS Software in the
U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia (&#147;Georgia Action&#148;). We
seek a declaration from the court that we have not infringed any valid claim of
the &#145;665 patent. By Order entered December&nbsp;16, 2004, Judge Koeltl of the
U.S. District Court for the Southern&nbsp;District of New York granted our
motion to transfer the New York Action to the Northern District of Georgia,
which has now consolidated the former New York Action with the Georgia Action.
On July&nbsp;7, 2005, the Court also granted STS leave to amend its complaint
to add three patents to the dispute, namely: U.S. Patent Nos. 6,865,604;
6,871,229; and 6,880,004 (respectively, &#147;the &#145;604 patent,&#148; &#147;the &#145;229&nbsp;patent,&#148;
and &#147;the &#145;004 patent&#148;; collectively, &#147;the STS patents&#148;), again seeking solely
injunctive relief. We answered the first amended complaint and asserted
counterclaims on July&nbsp;29, 2005, collectively, through which we deny
infringement of any valid claim of the STS patents and seek a declaration to
that effect. The case has been set on a discovery calendar and is at a
preliminary stage.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;30, 2004,
we filed in the United States District Court for the Northern District of
Georgia, Atlanta Division, a lawsuit against NICE Systems,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;NICE
Inc.&#148;), a wholly-owned subsidiary of NICE&nbsp;Ltd., alleging patent
infringement. Specifically, we have alleged that NICE products, including the
NiceUniverse products that include screen capture and synchronized screen and
voice capture technologies, infringe claims of U.S. Patent Nos. 5,790,798 (&#147;the
&#145;798 Patent&#148;) and 6,510,220 (&#147;the &#145;220&nbsp;Patent&#148;), both entitled &#147;Method and
Apparatus for Simultaneously Monitoring Computer User Screen and Telephone
Activity from a Remote Location.&#148; We have sought an injunction and money
damages for NICE&#146;s infringement of these two patents. NICE Inc. has answered
and counterclaimed for declaratory judgments of non-infringement and
invalidity. Since then, on February&nbsp;24, 2005, we filed suit against
NICE&nbsp;Ltd. because of its infringing activities in violation of the &#145;798
and &#145;220 patents, including importation of the accused NICE products. By order
dated April&nbsp;5, 2005, Judge Pannell has consolidated the NICE Inc. and NICE
Ltd. actions. The case has been set on a modified discovery calendar after
consolidation and is at a preliminary stage.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2001, IEX
Corporation filed a lawsuit against Blue Pumpkin in the United States District
Court for the Eastern District of Texas, Sherman Division, alleging that Blue
Pumpkin infringed IEX&nbsp;Corporation&#146;s (&#147;IEX&#148;) U.S. Patent No.&nbsp;6,044,355
(&#147;the &#145;355 Patent&#148;) by making and selling certain workforce management and call
routing software products, including Blue Pumpkin&#146;s Prime Time Skills and Prime
Time Enterprise products. IEX&#146;s lawsuit seeks actual damages, an award of
treble damages pursuant to 35 U.S.C. &#167; 284, an award of prejudgment interest,
costs, and attorney&#146;s fees, and an injunction against Blue Pumpkin&#146;s making or
selling the products that IEX claims infringe its &#145;355 Patent.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;4, 2005,
Blue Pumpkin filed in the United States District Court for the Northern
District of Georgia, Atlanta Division, a lawsuit against IEX Corporation
alleging patent infringement. Specifically, Blue Pumpkin has alleged that IEX
products infringe claims of Blue Pumpkin&#146;s U.S. Patent No.&nbsp;6,952,732 (&#147;the
&#145;732 Patent&#148;), entitled &#147;Method and apparatus for multi-contact scheduling.&#148;
Blue Pumpkin&#146;s lawsuit seeks an injunction and money damages for IEX&#146;s
infringement of the &#145;732 Patent.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">34</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">WITNESS SYSTEMS,&nbsp;INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)<br> December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;15, 2005,
IEX and Blue Pumpkin reached a tentative agreement to settle all claims
asserted between them in both the Texas and Georgia cases, subject to a number
of contingencies including negotiation, execution and delivery by the parties
of a definite settlement agreement prior to a deadline established by the
court, currently March&nbsp;15, 2006. The terms of the settlement agreement are
confidential. We expect to recover more than half of the settlement amount and
related litigation costs from the escrow fund that was established with a
portion of the purchase price in connection with our acquisition of Blue Pumpkin.
As at December&nbsp;31, 2005, we have accrued the balance of the anticipated
settlement costs and do not expect that the settlement will require any
additional material charges. (See&nbsp;Note 5 to the Consolidated Financial
Statements included elsewhere in this report for discussion of the Blue Pumpkin
acquisition).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">While we currently expect
to reach a definitive settlement with IEX, a number of terms that we view as
significant remain under negotiation, and we cannot assure you that we will be
able to reach a definitive settlement agreement on terms acceptable to us. If a
definitive settlement agreement is not reached, the litigations between IEX and
Blue Pumpkin will go forward. In the case of IEX&#146;s lawsuit against Blue
Pumpkin, a trial date will be set by the court, most likely in the late spring
of 2006. Blue Pumpkin&#146;s lawsuit against IEX is in a more preliminary stage and
would be unlikely to reach trial before 2007. If the litigations proceed to
trial, we intend to defend against IEX&#146;s claims vigorously and to pursue Blue
Pumpkin&#146;s claims against IEX vigorously, but we are unable to predict the
outcome of either case or to assess what, if any, impact an adverse result
would have on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;25, 2005,
Blue Pumpkin filed in the Tokyo District Court a lawsuit against P&amp;W
Solutions Co., Ltd. (&#147;P&amp;W&#148;) alleging that P&amp;W has infringed copyrights
in Blue Pumpkin Director Enterprise Version 33 software. P&amp;W has filed an
answer, and the case is at a preliminary stage.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;19, 2006,
we filed in the United States District Court for the Northern District of
Georgia, Atlanta Division, a lawsuit against NICE Systems,&nbsp;Inc. and NICE
Systems, Ltd. (collectively &#147;NICE&#148;), alleging patent infringement. Specifically,
we have alleged that NICE products, including NicePerform and related products
that include the ability to monitor communications to detect the presence of at
least one predetermined parameter, infringe claims of our U.S. Patent No.&nbsp;6,404,857
B1 (&#147;the &#145;857 Patent&#148;), entitled &#147;Signal Monitoring Apparatus for Analyzing
Communications.&#148; We have sought an injunction and money damages for NICE&#146;s
infringement of the &#145;857 patent. NICE has not yet responded to the complaint,
and this case is at a preliminary stage. .</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are not party to any
litigation or other legal proceedings that we believe could have a material
adverse effect on our business, operating results or financial condition.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Indemnifications and Warranties&#151;</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">We </font></i></b></font>more
often than not indemnify our customers against damages and costs resulting from
claims of patent, copyright, or trademark infringement associated with use of
our software in its software licensing agreements. We have historically not
made any payments under such indemnifications. However, we continue to monitor
the conditions that are subject to the indemnifications to identify whether it
is probable that a loss has occurred, and would recognize any such losses under
the indemnifications when those losses are probable and estimable. In addition,
we warrant to customers that our software products operate substantially in
accordance with the software product&#146;s specifications. Historically, no costs
have been incurred related to software product warranties and none are expected
in the future, and as such no accruals for warranty costs have been made.<a name="ValuationAndQualifyingAccountsinT_145830"></a></p>
